HSTU’s original 2024 experiments use sampled softmax with 128 negatives on MovieLens and 512 on Amazon Books, supporting multi-negative training as a family-consistent baseline; these results do not establish an optimal count for the four target categories. [HSTU paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3). WWW 2026’s R²NS directly supports curriculum sampling: uniform-negative warm-start, followed by progressively harder sampling with stochastic selection among high-scoring candidates. Its experiments show that introducing hard negatives too early can underperform uniform sampling; highest-scoring unobserved items can also be false negatives. These findings support the hypothesis, but do not establish gains for HSTU or lexical sampling specifically. [R²NS](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf).

HSTU-BLaIR (2025) adds textual representations while explicitly retaining uniform item-ID sampling; it provides no direct evidence that title-neighbor mining improves HSTU. Its pretrained embeddings are outside this task’s permitted resources. [HSTU-BLaIR](https://kdd2025llm4ecommerce.github.io/assets/accepted/13_HSTU_BLaIR_Lightweight_Cont.pdf). A task-compatible experimental inference: compare uniform multi-negative sampled-softmax training against the same HSTU with a gradually introduced, capped fraction of moderately similar title negatives. Match negative count and compute; exclude padding, the target, and all observed training positives. Retain uniform coverage and randomize candidate selection rather than always choosing the closest title or highest score. Lexical similarity supplies candidate difficulty, not evidence of dislike; excluding known positives cannot eliminate latent false negatives. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10, with one trained HSTU per category.
